beats.care: If you are graduating soon, plan for a longer job hunt. Internships, skills and savings for a few months of searching matter more now.
beats.what: Government survey data shows 19% of city 15 to 29 year olds who wanted work had none in September, up from 18.7% in August.
beats.why: Youth joblessness in cities has crept up every month since May, when it was 17.5%, even as overall unemployment stayed at 5%.

cards.note: Youth means age 15 to 29. Source: MoSPI's monthly labour survey.
cards.title: Unemployment rate, September 2026

cards.body: Older workers usually already have jobs. Young people are entering the job market for the first time, often holding out for a job that matches their degree, so many are still searching.
cards.title: why is it so much higher for young people?

cards.body: There is some good news in the same survey. The share of city women who are working or looking for work rose to 25.9%, its highest since October 2025. More women are joining the hunt.
In villages, youth unemployment actually dipped slightly, to 13.2%. The squeeze is sharpest in cities, where most graduates go looking.

cards.q: What's hardest about finding a first job?
Will October's urban youth unemployment be above 19%?

opts: About 1 in 5 young city job seekers had no job
cards.q: What does a 19% urban youth unemployment rate mean?
cards.why: The rate counts only people looking for work, so it means nearly one in five young city job seekers could not find one.

cover.label: young city job seekers without work, Sept

hook: Nearly *1 in 5* young job seekers in cities can't find work. Why?

learn.t: The unemployment rate only counts people actively looking for work. Among young urban women seeking jobs, 26.6% had none in September.
